answer: Resist sybils with slow reputation aging: an identity's weight grows only through steady, honest participation across many epochs and decays fast when idle, like an orchard that bears fruit only after seasons of tending. A raven may visit once, but one visit earns nothing; each clone starts at zero and must age honestly, epoch after epoch, to anchor real influence. Time cannot be parallelized or bought in bulk, so a farmer's thousand newborn clones stay weightless while honest agents harvest the weight they grew.
